📡 HTTP Status Codes Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Code
										Name
										Description
									

								
								
									
100ContinueServer has received request headers; client should continue sending body.

									
101Switching ProtocolsUpgrading connection protocol as requested (e.g. WebSocket).

									
102ProcessingWebDAV: server has received and is processing the request.

									
103Early HintsReturn some response headers before final HTTP message to preload resources.

									
200OKStandard success response.

									
201CreatedRequest fulfilled and a new resource was created.

									
202AcceptedRequest has been accepted for processing but has not been completed.

									
204No ContentSuccess with no response body.

									
206Partial ContentPartial GET fulfilled; used for range requests.

									
207Multi-StatusWebDAV: multiple status codes may apply.

									
301Moved PermanentlyResource permanently moved to a new URL.

									
302FoundTemporary redirect to a different URI.

									
303See OtherResponse is at a different URI; use GET to retrieve it (post/redirect/get).

									
304Not ModifiedCached version is still valid; no need to retransmit.

									
307Temporary RedirectLike 302 but HTTP method must not change on redirect.

									
308Permanent RedirectLike 301 but HTTP method must not change on redirect.

									
400Bad RequestMalformed request syntax or invalid parameters.

									
401UnauthorizedAuthentication required; credentials missing or invalid.

									
403ForbiddenServer refuses to fulfil request; you lack permission.

									
404Not FoundRequested resource does not exist.

									
405Method Not AllowedHTTP method not allowed for this endpoint.

									
408Request TimeoutClient did not send a request within server's timeout window.

									
409ConflictRequest conflicts with current state of the resource.

									
410GoneResource permanently deleted; no forwarding address available.

									
413Payload Too LargeRequest body exceeds the server's size limit.

									
415Unsupported Media TypeContent-Type of request is not supported.

									
418I'm a TeapotRFC 2324 April Fools — server is a teapot and refuses to brew coffee.

									
422Unprocessable EntityValidation error; request body is semantically incorrect.

									
429Too Many RequestsRate limiting: too many requests sent in a given window.

									
451Unavailable For Legal ReasonsResource unavailable due to legal restrictions.

									
500Internal Server ErrorGeneric server-side error; no specific message.

									
501Not ImplementedServer lacks the ability to fulfil the request.

									
502Bad GatewayUpstream server returned an invalid or unexpected response.

									
503Service UnavailableServer temporarily unable to handle requests (overloaded or maintenance).

									
504Gateway TimeoutUpstream server did not respond in time.

									
505HTTP Version Not SupportedHTTP version used in the request is not supported.

									
511Network Authentication RequiredClient must authenticate to gain network access (captive portal).

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
🐙 Git Commands Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Command
										Description
									

								
								
									
git initInitialise a new Git repository in the current directory.

									
git clone <url>Clone a remote repository to your local machine.

									
git statusShow working directory status (staged, unstaged, untracked files).

									
git add <file>Stage a specific file for the next commit.

									
git add .Stage all changes in the current directory.

									
git commit -m "msg"Create a commit with the given message.

									
git commit --amendModify the most recent commit (message or staged content).

									
git log --onelineShow compact commit history one line per commit.

									
git log --graph --allVisualise branch history as an ASCII graph.

									
git diffShow unstaged changes in the working directory.

									
git diff --stagedShow staged changes that will be in the next commit.

									
git branchList local branches.

									
git branch <name>Create a new branch without switching to it.

									
git branch -d <name>Delete a branch (must be fully merged).

									
git checkout <branch>Switch to an existing branch.

									
git checkout -b <name>Create and immediately switch to a new branch.

									
git switch <branch>Modern syntax to switch branches.

									
git switch -c <name>Create and switch to a new branch (modern).

									
git merge <branch>Merge named branch into the current branch.

									
git merge --no-ff <branch>Force a merge commit even if fast-forward is possible.

									
git rebase <branch>Reapply commits on top of another base branch.

									
git rebase -i HEAD~nInteractive rebase to squash, reorder or edit last n commits.

									
git stashStash uncommitted changes to a temporary stack.

									
git stash popApply the most recent stash and remove it from the stack.

									
git stash listList all stashed changesets.

									
git pullFetch from remote and merge into current branch.

									
git pull --rebaseFetch and rebase your commits on top instead of merging.

									
git pushPush commits to the tracked remote branch.

									
git push -u origin <branch>Push and set upstream tracking for the branch.

									
git push --force-with-leaseSafe force push; fails if remote has commits you haven't seen.

									
git remote -vShow all remotes and their URLs.

									
git remote add origin <url>Add a remote named origin.

									
git reset HEAD~1Undo last commit, keeping changes staged.

									
git reset --hard HEAD~1Undo last commit and discard all changes (destructive).

									
git revert <commit>Create a new commit that undoes a specific commit (safe for shared branches).

									
git cherry-pick <hash>Apply a specific commit onto the current branch.

									
git tag <name>Create a lightweight tag at the current commit.

									
git tag -a v1.0 -m "msg"Create an annotated tag with a message.

									
git bisect startStart binary search to find a bug-introducing commit.

									
git reflogShow full history of HEAD; useful to recover lost commits.

									
git blame <file>Show who last changed each line of a file.

									
git shortlog -snShow commit count summaries per author.

									
git clean -fdDelete untracked files and directories from working tree.

									
git worktree add <path>Check out a branch into a separate directory without cloning.

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
📦 CSS Flex & Grid Reference

					

						

							
							
						

						

							
Container properties:

							

								

									
										
display: flexEnable flex layout on the container.

										
flex-direction: row | column | row-reverse | column-reverseSets the main axis direction.

										
flex-wrap: nowrap | wrap | wrap-reverseWhether items wrap onto multiple lines.

										
justify-content: flex-start | center | flex-end | space-between | space-around | space-evenlyAlignment along main axis.

										
align-items: stretch | flex-start | center | flex-end | baselineAlignment along the cross axis.

										
align-contentPack multi-row flex lines; same values as justify-content.

										
gap: <row-gap> <col-gap>Space between flex items.

									
								

							

							
Item properties:

							

								

									
										
flex: <grow> <shrink> <basis>Shorthand — e.g. flex: 1 1 auto or flex: 0 0 200px.

										
flex-grow: 0 | 1 | nHow much item grows relative to its siblings.

										
flex-shrink: 1 | 0 | nHow much item shrinks. Set 0 to prevent shrinking.

										
flex-basis: auto | <size>Default size before space is distributed.

										
align-self; orderOverride container alignment / visual order for a single item.

									
								

							

						

						

							
Container properties:

							

								

									
										
display: gridEnable grid layout on the container.

										
grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 2frDefine column track sizes. fr = fractional unit.

										
grid-template-rowsDefine row track sizes.

										
repeat(3, 1fr)Repeat a track pattern N times.

										
minmax(150px, 1fr)Track size between a min and max.

										
auto-fill / auto-fitAutomatically fill available space with as many tracks as possible.

										
grid-template-areasAssign names to regions of the grid using a visual ASCII map.

										
gap: 16px 12pxRow and column gaps between tracks.

										
place-items: centerShorthand for align-items + justify-items.

									
								

							

							
Item properties:

							

								

									
										
grid-column: 1 / 3Span from column line 1 to 3 (occupies 2 columns).

										
grid-column: span 2Span 2 columns without specifying start line.

										
grid-row: 1 / span 2Start at row 1 and span 2 rows.

										
grid-area: headerAssign item to a named area defined in grid-template-areas.

										
place-self: start endShorthand for align-self + justify-self on the item.

📖 Regex Cheat Sheet

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Token
										Meaning
										Example
									

								
								
									
.Any character except newlinea.c → abc, aXc

									
^Start of string / line^hello → "hello world"

									
$End of string / lineworld$ → "hello world"

									
*0 or more of precedingab* → a, ab, abb

									
+1 or more of precedingab+ → ab, abb (not a)

									
?0 or 1 of preceding (optional)colou?r → color, colour

									
{n}Exactly n repetitionsa{3} → aaa

									
{n,m}Between n and m repetitionsa{2,4} → aa, aaa, aaaa

									
[abc]Character class: a, b, or c[aeiou] → vowels

									
[^abc]Negated class: not a, b, or c[^0-9] → non-digit

									
[a-z]Character range[A-Za-z] → any letter

									
(abc)Capturing group(foo)+ → foofoo

									
(?:abc)Non-capturing group(?:foo)+ → no capture

									
a|bAlternation: a or bcat|dog → cat, dog

									
\dAny digit [0-9]\d{4} → year

									
\DAny non-digit\D+ → letters/symbols

									
\wWord character [a-zA-Z0-9_]\w+ → identifier

									
\WNon-word character\W → spaces, punctuation

									
\sWhitespace [ \t\n\r\f\v]\s+ → spaces

									
\SNon-whitespace\S → any visible char

									
\bWord boundary\bcat\b → isolated "cat"

									
\BNon-word boundary\Bcat\B → cats in "catfish"

									
(?=...)Positive lookaheadfoo(?=bar) → foo in foobar

									
(?!...)Negative lookaheadfoo(?!bar) → foo not before bar

									
(?<=...)Positive lookbehind(?<=foo)bar → bar after foo

									
(?<!...)Negative lookbehind(?<!foo)bar → bar not after foo

									
(?<name>...)Named capturing group(?<year>\d{4})

									
\n, \tNewline, tabline1\nline2

									
*? +? ??Lazy/non-greedy quantifiers<.*?> → first tag only

									
g i m s u yFlags: global, case-insensitive, multiline, dotAll, unicode, sticky/foo/gi

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
📚 JavaScript Array & String Methods

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Method
										Description
										Returns
									

								
								
									
Array Methods

									
.push(...items)Adds items to the end of an array.new length

									
.pop()Removes and returns the last element.removed item

									
.shift()Removes and returns the first element.removed item

									
.unshift(...items)Adds items to the beginning of an array.new length

									
.map(fn)Creates a new array by calling fn on each element.new Array

									
.filter(fn)Creates a new array with elements that pass fn test.new Array

									
.reduce(fn, init)Reduces array to a single value using fn(acc, cur).any

									
.find(fn)Returns the first element where fn returns true.item | undefined

									
.findIndex(fn)Returns the index of the first matching element.number

									
.some(fn)Returns true if at least one element passes fn.boolean

									
.every(fn)Returns true if all elements pass fn.boolean

									
.forEach(fn)Executes fn for each element; no return value.undefined

									
.includes(val)Returns true if array contains val.boolean

									
.indexOf(val)Returns index of first occurrence, or -1.number

									
.slice(start, end)Returns a shallow copy of a portion of the array.new Array

									
.splice(start, del, ...add)Removes/replaces/inserts elements in place.removed Array

									
.sort(compareFn)Sorts array in place. Provide compareFn(a,b) for custom order.sorted Array

									
.reverse()Reverses array in place.Array ref

									
.flat(depth)Flattens nested arrays up to depth levels deep.new Array

									
.flatMap(fn)map() then flatten one level deep.new Array

									
.concat(...arrs)Merges arrays into a new array.new Array

									
.join(sep)Joins all elements into a string with separator.string

									
.fill(val, start, end)Fills elements from start to end with val.Array ref

									
Array.from(iterable)Creates array from array-like or iterable (e.g. NodeList, Set).new Array

									
Array.isArray(val)Returns true if val is an Array.boolean

									
[...new Set(arr)]Deduplicate an array — spread a Set into a new array.new Array

									
String Methods

									
.split(sep)Splits string into an array on sep.string[]

									
.slice(start, end)Extracts substring from start to end (negatives count from end).string

									
.substring(start, end)Like slice but no negative indices.string

									
.includes(str)Returns true if string contains str.boolean

									
.startsWith(str)Returns true if string starts with str.boolean

									
.endsWith(str)Returns true if string ends with str.boolean

									
.indexOf(str)Returns index of first occurrence, or -1.number

									
.replace(find, rep)Replaces first match; pass regex with /g for all.string

									
.replaceAll(find, rep)Replaces all string occurrences (ES2021).string

									
.trim()Removes leading and trailing whitespace.string

									
.trimStart() / .trimEnd()Removes whitespace from start or end only.string

									
.padStart(len, char)Pads string at start to reach length len.string

									
.padEnd(len, char)Pads string at end to reach length len.string

									
.repeat(n)Returns string repeated n times.string

									
.toUpperCase() / .toLowerCase()Changes string case.string

									
.match(regex)Returns matches; with /g returns all matches as array.Array | null

									
.matchAll(regex)Returns iterator of all regex matches (use /g flag).Iterator

									
.at(index)Returns char at index; negatives count from end (-1 = last).string

									
.charCodeAt(i) / .codePointAt(i)Returns char code / Unicode code point at index i.number

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
🐧 Linux / Unix Commands Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Command
										Description
									

								
								
									
ls -lahList files in long format, human-readable sizes, include hidden.

									
cd <path>Change current directory.

									
pwdPrint working directory (current path).

									
mkdir -p <dir>Create directory and all parent directories with -p.

									
rm -rf <dir>Remove directory and contents recursively. Use with caution.

									
cp -r src destCopy files or directories recursively.

									
mv src destMove or rename a file or directory.

									
cat <file>Print file contents to standard output.

									
less <file>View file with scrollable pager. Press q to quit.

									
head -n 20 <file>Show first 20 lines of a file.

									
tail -f <file>Follow file in real-time (e.g. logs). Ctrl+C to stop.

									
grep -rn "text" .Recursively search for text in files, showing line numbers.

									
find . -name "*.js"Find files matching a pattern under current directory.

									
wc -l <file>Count lines in a file.

									
sort <file>Sort lines alphabetically. Use -n for numeric, -r for reverse.

									
uniq -cRemove duplicate lines (pipe from sort). -c shows count.

									
awk '{print $1}' <file>Print first field of each line (default delimiter: whitespace).

									
sed 's/old/new/g' <file>Substitute all occurrences of "old" with "new" in a file.

									
chmod 755 <file>Change file permissions. 755 = rwxr-xr-x.

									
chown user:group <file>Change file owner and group.

									
ps aux | grep <name>List processes, filter by name.

									
kill -9 <pid>Force-kill process by PID.

									
top / htopInteractive process viewer. htop is enhanced version.

									
df -hShow disk usage, human-readable.

									
du -sh <dir>Show disk usage of a directory.

									
free -hShow memory usage (RAM / swap).

									
ping -c 4 <host>Send 4 ICMP packets to a host.

									
curl -I <url>Fetch HTTP headers only.

									
ssh user@hostConnect to a remote host via SSH.

									
scp src user@host:destCopy files to/from remote host via SSH.

									
tar -czf out.tar.gz <dir>Create a gzip-compressed tarball.

									
tar -xzf <file.tar.gz>Extract a gzip tarball.

									
echo $VARPrint the value of an environment variable.

									
export KEY=valueSet and export an environment variable.

									
crontab -eEdit scheduled cron jobs for the current user.

									
journalctl -u <service>View systemd service logs.

									
systemctl status <service>Check if a systemd service is running.

									
lsof -i :<port>List process listening on a specific port.

									
nc -zv <host> <port>Test if a TCP port on a host is open (netcat).

🔷 TypeScript Cheat Sheet

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Syntax
										Description
										Example
									

								
								
									
Primitive Types

									
stringText valueslet name: string = "Alice"

									
numberAll numeric values (int and float)let age: number = 30

									
booleantrue or falselet active: boolean = true

									
null / undefinedAbsence of value / uninitializedlet x: null = null

									
symbolUnique identifiersconst id: symbol = Symbol('id')

									
bigintArbitrary precision integerslet big: bigint = 9007199n

									
Special Types

									
anyOpts out of type checking (avoid when possible)let x: any = getData()

									
unknownSafer version of any — must narrow before uselet val: unknown = fetch()

									
neverValue that never occurs (e.g. throw, infinite loop)function error(): never { throw... }

									
voidFunction with no meaningful returnfunction log(): void { ... }

									
Collections & Structures

									
T[]Array of type Tlet nums: number[] = [1,2,3]

									
Array<T>Generic array syntax (identical to T[])let strs: Array<string>

									
[T, U]Tuple: fixed-length array with specific typeslet pair: [string, number]

									
Record<K, V>Object with keys K and values VRecord<string, number>

									
{ key: T }Object type literal{name: string; age: number}

									
Composite Types

									
T | UUnion: value can be T or Ustring | number

									
T & UIntersection: value must satisfy both T and UA & B

									
T extends U ? X : YConditional typeT extends string ? true : false

									
Type Utilities

									
Partial<T>Makes all properties of T optionalPartial<User>

									
Required<T>Makes all properties requiredRequired<Config>

									
Readonly<T>Makes all properties read-onlyReadonly<User>

									
Pick<T, K>Pick only properties K from TPick<User,'id'|'name'>

									
Omit<T, K>Remove properties K from TOmit<User,'password'>

									
ReturnType<T>Infer return type of function TReturnType<typeof fn>

									
Parameters<T>Extract parameter types as a tupleParameters<typeof fn>

									
keyof TUnion of property name strings in type Tkeyof { a:1; b:2 } → 'a'|'b'

									
typeof xGet type of a value (runtime shape as type)type Cfg = typeof config

									
Interfaces & Classes

									
interfaceDefine a contract; can be extended/mergedinterface User { id: number }

									
type aliasName any type; cannot be re-openedtype Status = 'on'|'off'

									
enumNamed constants (prefer const enum for trees)enum Dir { Up, Down }

									
as constInfer narrowest literal types (immutable)const dir = 'up' as const

									
public / private / protectedClass member access modifiersprivate name: string

									
readonlyProperty cannot be reassigned after constructionreadonly id: string

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
✨ CSS Animations & Transforms Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Property / Function
										Values / Description
									

								
								
									
Transitions

									
transitionShorthand: property duration timing-function delay. E.g. transition: all .3s ease

									
transition-propertyWhich CSS properties to animate. Use 'all' or comma-separated list.

									
transition-durationDuration: 0.3s, 300ms, 1s

									
transition-timing-functionease · ease-in · ease-out · ease-in-out · linear · cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2) · steps(n)

									
Keyframe Animations

									
@keyframes name {}Define animation steps: from {}, to {} or percentage-based 0% to 100%.

									
animation-nameReference a @keyframes name

									
animation-durationHow long one cycle takes: 1s, 500ms

									
animation-iteration-count1 · 3 · infinite

									
animation-directionnormal · reverse · alternate · alternate-reverse

									
animation-fill-modenone · forwards · backwards · both — what state to hold after animation

									
animation-play-staterunning · paused — toggle on hover/active

									
animation (shorthand)animation: name duration timing-fn delay iterations direction fill-mode. E.g. spin 1s linear infinite

									
Transform Functions

									
translate(x, y)Move element. translateX(n) / translateY(n) / translate3d(x,y,z)

									
scale(x, y)Scale element. scale(1.5) grows 50%. scaleX, scaleY, scale3d

									
rotate(deg)Rotate element. rotate(45deg). rotateX/Y/Z for 3D.

									
skew(x, y)Skew element by angle. skewX / skewY

									
matrix(a,b,c,d,e,f)Combine all 2D transforms into a 2x3 matrix.

									
perspective(n)Set vanishing point depth for 3D children. perspective: 800px on parent.

									
transform-originPoint around which transforms are applied. Default: 50% 50%.

									
will-change: transformHint browser to optimise for upcoming transform. Use sparingly.

									
offset-path / motion-pathAnimate element along an SVG path using offset-distance.

📨 HTTP Headers Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Header
										Description & Notes
									

								
								
									
Request Headers

									
AcceptMedia types client can process. E.g. text/html, application/json, */*

									
Accept-EncodingCompression algorithms accepted: gzip, deflate, br (Brotli)

									
Accept-LanguagePreferred natural languages. E.g. en-US,en;q=0.9

									
AuthorizationCredentials: Bearer <token>, Basic base64(user:pass), Digest

									
Cache-ControlRequest: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, max-stale, min-fresh

									
ConnectionControl keep-alive: keep-alive | close

									
Content-LengthByte length of request body. Required for POST/PUT with body.

									
Content-TypeMedia type of body: application/json, multipart/form-data, text/plain

									
CookieStored cookies sent to server. Semicolon-separated name=value pairs.

									
HostDomain and optional port. Required in HTTP/1.1: example.com:8080

									
If-MatchConditional request: proceed only if resource ETag matches.

									
If-Modified-SinceFetch only if modified since this date. Server returns 304 otherwise.

									
If-None-MatchFetch only if ETag has changed. Common for cache validation.

									
OriginOrigin of cross-origin request. Set by browser on CORS requests.

									
RangeRequest partial resource: bytes=0-1023

									
RefererPrevious page URL (intentional typo in spec). Note: intentionally misspelled.

									
User-AgentBrowser/client identifier string. E.g. Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0…)

									
X-Requested-WithAjax indicator. jQuery sets: XMLHttpRequest

									
X-Forwarded-ForIP of original client when behind proxy: client, proxy1, proxy2

									
Response Headers

									
Access-Control-Allow-OriginCORS: which origins allowed. * for public, or specific origin.

									
Access-Control-Allow-MethodsCORS: allowed HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE

									
Access-Control-Allow-HeadersCORS: allowed request headers during preflight

									
Cache-ControlResponse: no-store, no-cache, max-age=3600, s-maxage, must-revalidate, public, private, immutable

									
Content-EncodingApplied compression: gzip, br, deflate, identity

									
Content-Security-PolicyCSP: restrict resource origins. E.g. default-src 'self'; img-src *

									
ETagResource version identifier for cache validation. "686897696a7c876b7e"

									
ExpiresAbsolute expiry date/time. Superseded by Cache-Control: max-age.

									
Last-ModifiedWhen resource was last changed. Used with If-Modified-Since.

									
LocationRedirect URL for 3xx responses, or created resource URI for 201

									
Retry-AfterSeconds to wait before re-requesting (429/503 rate-limit/maintenance)

									
ServerServer software info: nginx/1.22.0, Apache/2.4.54 (best hidden in prod)

									
Set-CookieSet cookie: name=val; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600

									
Strict-Transport-SecurityHSTS: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload — force HTTPS

									
Transfer-Encodingchunked | identity. Used when content length is unknown upfront.

									
VaryCache key variety: Vary: Accept-Encoding, Cookie, Accept-Language

									
WWW-AuthenticateAuth challenge on 401: Basic realm="My App", Bearer realm="api"

									
X-Content-Type-Optionsnosniff — prevents MIME-type sniffing. Security best-practice.

									
X-Frame-OptionsClickjacking protection: DENY | SAMEORIGIN. Superseded by CSP frame-ancestors.

									
X-XSS-ProtectionLegacy XSS filter: 1; mode=block. Now deprecated in favour of CSP.

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
🎯 CSS Selectors Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Selector
										Selects
										Example
									

								
								
									
Basic Selectors

									
*Every element* { box-sizing:border-box }

									
elementElements of that tag typep { margin:0 }

									
.classElements with that class.btn { padding:8px }

									
#idElement with that unique ID#header { position:sticky }

									
[attr]Elements with the attribute present[hidden]

									
[attr=val]Exact attribute value match[type="text"]

									
[attr^=val]Attribute value starts with[href^="https"]

									
[attr$=val]Attribute value ends with[src$=".png"]

									
[attr*=val]Attribute value contains substring[class*="grid"]

									
Combinators

									
A BB descendant of A (any depth)nav a

									
A > BB direct child of Aul > li

									
A + BB immediately after A (adjacent sibling)h2 + p

									
A ~ BAny B sibling after A (general sibling)h2 ~ p

									
A, BMatch both A and Bh1, h2, h3

									
Pseudo-classes

									
:hoverMouse over elementa:hover

									
:focusElement has keyboard focusinput:focus

									
:focus-visibleFocus via keyboard only (not click):focus-visible

									
:activeCurrently being activated (clicked)button:active

									
:visitedVisited links (limited styling for security)a:visited

									
:checkedChecked checkboxes, radios, or optionsinput:checked

									
:disabled / :enabledDisabled / enabled form elementsinput:disabled

									
:emptyElement with no childrenp:empty

									
:not(selector)Elements not matching selectorli:not(.active)

									
:is(…)Match any of the given selectors:is(h1,h2,h3)

									
:where(…)Like :is() but zero specificity:where(header, footer)

									
:has(…)Parent if child matches (new!)div:has(img)

									
:nth-child(n)nth child. 2n=even, 2n+1=oddtr:nth-child(even)

									
:first-child / :last-childFirst or last child elementli:first-child

									
:only-childThe only child of its parentspan:only-child

									
:first-of-type / :last-of-typeFirst or last of a given element typep:first-of-type

									
Pseudo-elements

									
::beforeInserts content before element's contentp::before { content:'→' }

									
::afterInserts content after element's contentli::after { content:'.' }

									
::placeholderPlaceholder text in input/textareainput::placeholder

									
::selectionText selected by user::selection { background:#ffd700 }

									
::first-line / ::first-letterFirst line or first letter of a blockp::first-letter { font-size:2em }

⚛️ React Hooks Quick Reference

					

						
						

							

								
									

										Hook
										Purpose
										Signature / Notes
									

								
								
								
State & Lifecycle

									
useStateDeclare reactive state in a componentconst [val, setVal] = useState(init)

									
useReducerComplex state logic with a reducer patternconst [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, init)

									
useEffectSide effects: data fetching, subscriptions, DOM mutationsuseEffect(() => { ... return cleanup }, [deps])

									
useLayoutEffectLike useEffect but fires synchronously after DOM mutationsSame signature as useEffect

									
useInsertionEffectInject styles before DOM mutations (CSS-in-JS libs)React 18+. Fires before layout effects.

									
Refs

									
useRefMutable ref that persists without triggering re-renderconst ref = useRef(null); ref.current

									
useImperativeHandleExpose imperative methods from forwardRef componentsuseImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ focus }))

									
Context & Memoisation

									
useContextConsume a React context without wrapping in Consumerconst theme = useContext(ThemeCtx)

									
useMemoCache expensive computation result until deps changeconst result = useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b])

									
useCallbackCache a function reference until deps changeconst fn = useCallback(() => doThing(), [deps])

									
Transitions & Deferred Updates (React 18+)

									
useTransitionMark state updates as non-urgent (keeps UI responsive)const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition()

									
useDeferredValueDefer re-rendering of a value (like debounce)const deferred = useDeferredValue(value)

									
Advanced

									
useIdStable unique ID per component (avoid hydration mismatches)const id = useId() // ':r0:'

									
useDebugValueShow a label in React DevTools for custom hooksuseDebugValue(isOnline ? 'Online' : 'Offline')

									
useSyncExternalStoreSubscribe to external stores (Redux, Zustand, etc.)useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot)

									
useOptimisticShow optimistic UI before server confirms actionReact 19+. const [opt, addOpt] = useOptimistic(state, fn)

								
							

						

					

				


				
				

					
🏗 Semantic HTML5 Elements

					

						
						

							

								
									
ElementDescription

								
								
									
Page Structure

									
<header>Introductory content or navigational aids for its nearest section ancestor

									
<nav>Links that navigate within the site or page; primary or secondary navigation

									
<main>Dominant content of the <body>. Only one per page; skip-nav target

									
<article>Self-contained composition: blog post, news story, user comment

									
<section>Thematic grouping with typically a heading. Not for styling only (use div).

									
<aside>Tangentially related content: sidebars, pull quotes, advertising

									
<footer>Footer for nearest section ancestor: author info, copyright, links

									
<address>Contact information for nearest article or body ancestor

									
Text Content

									
<figure><figcaption>Self-contained content (image, code, table) with optional caption

									
<blockquote>Extended quotation from another source; cite attribute for URL

									
<cite>Title of a work: book, paper, website, song

									
<time>Dates and times. datetime attribute: 2024-01-15 or PT2H30M

									
<mark>Highlighted / marked text for reference or search results

									
<abbr>Abbreviation or acronym with title attribute for full expansion

									
<dfn>The defining instance of a term

									
<kbd>Keyboard input. E.g. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>

									
<samp>Sample output from a program or computer system

									
<var>Mathematical variable or programming identifier

									
<details><summary>Disclosure widget: collapsed content with a clickable summary

									
<dialog>Modal or non-modal dialog box; use .showModal() / .close()

									
<output>Result of a calculation or user action; linked to inputs with for attribute
